title: Understand Exam Score Tables
learning_objective: Learn how students and exam scores connect before writing exclusion logic.

tutorial.explanation: Many interview problems split names and activity rows into separate tables. Join students to exams when you need student names together with exam activity.
tutorial.syntax: SELECT s.student_id, s.student_name, COUNT(e.exam_id) AS exams_taken FROM students s INNER JOIN exams e ON s.student_id = e.student_id GROUP BY s.student_id, s.student_name;
tutorial.mental_model: The students table tells you who exists. The exams table tells you what happened. The join lets you ask questions about students who have exam rows.

guided_example.prompt: Count how many exams each participating student took.
guided_example.solution_query: SELECT s.student_id, s.student_name, COUNT(e.exam_id) AS exams_taken FROM students s INNER JOIN exams e ON s.student_id = e.student_id GROUP BY s.student_id, s.student_name;
guided_example.explanation: INNER JOIN keeps students who have matching exam rows. COUNT then counts exam rows per student.

practice.prompt: Return student_name and score for every exam row.
practice.expected_query: SELECT s.student_name, e.score FROM students s INNER JOIN exams e ON s.student_id = e.student_id;

hints: Join students to exams on student_id.
